brief: Goldman's Tony Pasquariello, head of hedge fund coverage, offers high level AI thoughts prefaced with humility. Hyperscaler capex was $154BN in 2023 and consensus for 2028 is over $1.3TN, so the market rightly obsesses over ROIC, and the bar to attach capex to durable revenue growth has risen. Proof moments landed in 2026 (META in Q4, GOOG and AMZN in Q1, MSFT and AMZN in Q2) but the buzz faded. His hypothesis: binary ROIC framing is too reductive, because AI also creates enterprise value by letting businesses operate better (cloud analogy) and through compulsory spend to protect a business (cyber analogy). This early in adoption precise ROIC is impossible, and George Lee holds returns may be set by competitive pressures with the value going to consumer surplus. Therefore pressure runs through every industry, some spend is low or no ROI yet necessary, and if those notions hold Corporate America stays on the gas. Against that: politics with the midterms as a cost-bearing litmus test, malevolence risk, and power provision, raising the risk of air pockets and dislocations akin to DeepSeek. Trend structurally higher, path more jagged. The publisher adds Morgan Stanley's read that token prices and server rental are falling.
